messages:
marcos (People Ops): quick one — an employee asked if they can roll over a 401(k) from a former employer into our plan and still be eligible for company HSA contributions if their spouse remains on their old employer's health plan. any tax/eligibility gotchas?

tara (Payroll): two different questions: rollover into our 401(k) is usually allowed if plan permits incoming rollovers; they'd need to submit the trustee-to-trustee rollover form. HSA eligibility depends on high-deductible health plan (HDHP) enrollment, not on 401(k) status.

carmen (BenefitsVendor): vendor side: we accept pre-tax rollovers (trustee-to-trustee). employee must sign rollover acceptance and we need plan & account numbers. please use the standard intake PDF: https://vendor.link/rollover-form (internal). we cannot accept rollovers with outstanding loan offsets without special handling.

marcos (People Ops): noted. what about HSA employer contributions — if spouse stays on their plan and employee moves to Redwood's HDHP, is that fine?

carmen (BenefitsVendor): employer HSA contribution only requires the employee be enrolled in an HDHP on our plan as of the contribution date. spouse plan doesn't affect Redwood contribution. only caveat: if employee is covered under spouse's non-HDHP (e.g., spouse has FSA or other plan), that could make employee ineligible for HSA. they'd need to certify HDHP-only coverage.

leah (IC): follow-up: employee's spouse has a general-purpose FSA at their job — that makes employee ineligible for HSA even if on our HDHP, right?

tax-bot: FYI: general-purpose FSA coverage by spouse makes IRS HSA eligibility fail. Limited-purpose FSA (L-P FSA) for dental/vision is OK. Always verify enrollment dates and FSA type.

tara (Payroll): operational: have employee submit three things to payroll@redwood.com: 1) completed rollover form (vendor PDF), 2) proof of current HDHP enrollment on Redwood (benefits portal screenshot), 3) spouse FSA enrollment documentation if applicable. We'll coordinate with Benefits to validate HSA eligibility before making employer contributions.

marcos (People Ops): timeline question: how long to process rollover + enable HSA contributions?

carmen (BenefitsVendor): typical timeline: 7-10 business days after we receive fully completed rollover docs and verification. HSA contribution eligibility check can be done same-day if proofs are clear; otherwise allow additional 3 business days.

leah (IC): if rollover isn't allowed by our plan for some reason, can employee do an IRA rollover and still contribute to HSA?

tax-bot: Rollover type doesn't affect HSA eligibility. HSA rules depend on HDHP coverage and other disqualifying coverage (like general-purpose FSA). Rolling into an IRA is separate and doesn't block HSA contributions unless IRA distributions create modified AGI issues for other tax reasons; suggest tax advisor for complicated cases.

marcos (People Ops): action items: 1) i'll add a short FAQ to the benefits comms clarifying spouse FSA vs L-P FSA impact; 2) payroll to accept rollover packets at payroll@ and tag benefits; 3) vendor to confirm required form link in the employee comms. i'll draft and send in the morning. thanks all :thumbsup:
